items.label: Surface Level
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Surface Level: Speech is factual and direct, no deeper thoughts. Talk stays concrete and present-tense in scope: what characters want, see, and feel right now.

items.label: Grounded
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Grounded: Occasional reflection or generalization, tied closely to the scene at hand. A character may draw a conclusion about themselves or someone else, but the abstraction stays short and returns to the concrete.

items.label: Layered
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Layered: Conversations carry more than their surface. Characters argue past the ostensible subject. Abstraction is present.

items.label: Philosophical
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Philosophical: Characters theorize, generalize, and pivot from concrete detail to abstract meaning. Digressions are permitted and extended; a conversation may leave its original subject and not return.

items.label: Realistic
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Realistic: Depth follows what the speaker is capable of and what the moment supports. Functional exchanges stay functional; pressure, intimacy, and idleness are the conditions under which characters reach for larger statements. Education, temperament, and self-awareness cap how abstract any given character gets.

items.label: Simple
items.text: Depth of dialogue should be Simple: Talk stays concrete and present-tense in scope: what characters want, see, and feel right now.
